texts.text: ... What's goin' on here?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Interior design renovation is underway at the Luxury Hall, as you can see.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Please watch your step.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Ah, apologies for the noise. This renovation is a rather large-scale construction project.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: ... "Renovation," eh?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: My old bossman used to say "grab yer tools, lads! We're headin' out to renovate a whole lotta mugs!" whenever we went after other Syndicates.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: That what you mean, lass?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Not exactly, no; this is just a very special refitting, quite unlike any before it—more than just switching out a few out-of-fashion displays. This time, the project is to build a cradle... in anticipation of the advent of a very important someone.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: I see now. This is when the Rouges attacked the Noirs, taking control of the Luxury Hall.
So... what're they eatin' back there? Some kinda cannibal feast?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: We are feasting on the Noir. Though this will hardly sate our hunger...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Please return once the construction work is complete. You will soon see this place reborn into a far grander state of beauty!
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: (She hums a nice tune, seemingly pleased with herself.)
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: ... It would be prudent to revisit the Luxury Hall once their "construction project" is completed.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: ... Huh. How'd you know they won't let us in, Clock?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <Oh, that’s…>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I'd been holding back on sharing the details of the loop with the Sinners, as doing so before I even understood how it worked might only plunge them into further uncertainty.
But now that we're this far in, maybe they could provide further insight if I kept them in the loop about... the loop.
Just as I was about to entertain that thought, a distant voice, breaking through an unfathomable stretch, cut through into my head.
<color=#515aee>You mustn't...</color>
<color=#515aee>Beset by... the gaze of the multitude...</color>
<color=#515aee>Lest your fate... be lost...</color>
... Has something occurred?
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: I must be the only one who can hear this voice.
<color=#515aee>Disclosing too much... risks... exposure...</color>
<color=#515aee>Then... cannot be... free from the... sunshine...</color>
<... Well, I just had this gut feeling that they probably won't let us in.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yeah? Fair enough, mate. I 'spose they didn't look like the friendliest sort even from a distance.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Raise your Prestige Rank first and come knocking again. Then, perhaps, we will reconsider your qualifications.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Hah! That's child's play, lass! Lookee, it ain't no trouble reaching my elbo—
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: —oooaagh! Blimey, where am I!?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: It appears that you have discovered the means of moving between the floors, Dante.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: *cough* So, what're we doin'?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <Well... I don't know. Since we can't enter the second floor proper...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... back to the restroom, you two... I guess?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oi, how do ya know that without givin' it a try? Don't go throwin' in the towel already.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Heathcliff, what Dante said is less out of despair and more—
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Yeah, whatever. Let's at least see what's goin' on here.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: A wall made of flesh and bone blocks the way. There are bodies of dead Noirs splayed around the floor past the wall.
We cannot go in this direction yet, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... We should've... been better prepared for our assault...
texts.speaker: Dying Noir

texts.text: If only... if only we could've... spread the news faster... Didn't have time... to assemble...
texts.speaker: Dying Noir

texts.text: Dammit... Damn it all...! We can't let the Rouges take the hall... They'll—they'll...
texts.speaker: Dying Noir

texts.text: <... Let's enter the Cradle.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: She lies dead still, but is wearing a peaceful smile—the same kind of smile only seen on the faces of those who know they have successfully carried out their duty to the end.
Aaah... At long last...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Please... I leave the rest... in your hands...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: <I don't know what'll happen when we get there, but... Let's try to find a way up to the fifth floor.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Regardless of what the Rouges want us to do, our goal is to get to the top floor of this building.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: In other words, you haven't yet reached the fifth floor and beyond.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <... No, I haven't.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Then your subsequent course of action should be to visit the fourth floor and seek a passage from there, Dante.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <Hm, yeah... But I should stop by the third floor before we do.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The third floor? Haven't you been there already?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: ... We've already decided to help the Rouges this time around. Might as well go all in and get on their good side.
<One of the employees on that floor really wanted to meet this... child. I thought it might be nice to have them meet.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Proceeding to the third floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Yeah, you do that. ... Oh, yeah. Better teach the kid manners now when you can, Clock! Else you'll never get the chance later, yeah? Remember that!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <What are you even talking about...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We proceeded to the third floor as Heathcliff continued to lecture us about the importance of early education.
A corpse.
<Let's... uh... do that?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Understood, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ugh, I hope this doesn't awaken somethin' horrid in there...
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: The Cradle quivers. Translucent blood vessels, radiating like the tendril roots of a plant, tremble in an irregular sway.
It almost looked like it was... breathing.
Meursault fed the piece of flesh into the cocoon. It suddenly jerked alive, jostling as though it had been waiting to receive it.
It appears that the membrane has... grown thinner.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <Something's flailing wildly in there... Is it trying to hatch?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Mm... though it has successfully punctured a small part of the membrane, emergence seems highly unlikely at this point.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Hang on, don't help it—let nature do its thing. I heard babies got to save themselves—
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Just as Heathcliff suggested that we leave it to fend for itself, the movement within the cocoon slowly began to subside.
Oh, bollocks. Oi, got anything sharp?! We gotta help, kid's startin' to go weak!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Perhaps we could use the pair of scissors obtained at the Alteration Shop.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Oh, you're right. Let's try cutting it open.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Manager, the piece of flesh has been emitting a rhythm akin to heartbeat ever since we first entered this floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Has it been getting stronger the closer we've gotten to the Cradle?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes. It appears to be a gradually intensifying resonance phenomenon of sorts.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That piece of flesh... It's got a similar feel to this cocoon-egg-thing, don't it?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Look, that's a mouth, innit? I think we're gonna have to feed this thing to that egg.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Your hypothesis carries merit. Faust concurs with that course of action.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Please... You must... the... cherished one...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Was this the one... who sang to me?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Well... That's what she told us.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: The face... it's smiling. Why...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Dunno... Maybe she were bloody over the moon, even with one foot in the grave.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: ... But why?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: She... wished for your birth and waited for it with anticipation.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Therefore, seeing you likely produced that happy smile, Pwie.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I don't understand. I didn't know her. She didn't... really know me either...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: And she was still happy?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... You're a right pain in the arse now you've learned how to talk...
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Some things just are. Grown-up stuff kids don't get.... Yeah, grown-up stuff.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: I'm going to grow soon.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Maybe I'll grow even bigger.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: So... I want to know more before I grow.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: When I'm learning new stuff... the cold goes away. I get to completely forget the empty something...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: That's why... I want to know. I want to know why she can smile even after dying...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... Instinct may lie at the root.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: The Rouges possess an instinct through which finding a new voice and following it fills an internal deficit.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: What's... "instinct"?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: It's a capacity or behavior that does not require instruction.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: An inclination that directs the subject of its own accord from the moment consciousness begins. One's nature, in some ways.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Then what is... my instinct?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: That is... unknown to us as well.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Many reach the end of life... without attaining a definitive understanding of their own essential nature...
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: A faint, contented smile hangs from her lips.
To die in service of others, of another... What kinds of emotions, experiences, and memories are capable of shaping a person into someone who so readily makes such a decision?
<More Noirs are coming this way...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We must bring the Brand Director's Golden Hide.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Yeah. Let's get inside.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: There's a piece of cloth and a Noir's note hidden by the base of the pillar.
<Hey, there's something written on this piece of cloth.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It says "The covetous Rouges have finally gone mad. The precious Golden Hide that preserves the Grand Magasin—they've—"
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Whoever wrote it didn't get to finish their message. Looks like they had to hide it in a hurry...
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: I stole a quick glance at the carnage being perpetrated on the other side of the wall before looking back at the piece of paper.
<... Let's take this with us, just in case it becomes relevant.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Eh? Back on this floor? Oi, bring in many eyeballs?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: We have earned enough.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ooh... Not a bad pull, CH!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <... She totally rubbed off on you, didn't she?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Mm. The guardian at the gate seems to have left. It is likely that the "interior design renovation" has ended.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <Things seem a little different from last time...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Huh... It's that big lass who was guarding the entrance.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: It was you... whom the Slumbering One... has asked me to hold out for...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: As the Brand Director... I was bestowed with the responsibility... to protect the noble Slumbering One. As the Brand Director... I held down this hall...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: The entity behind you must be the source of the Voice.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Yes. This is the Cradle... the garden of our ceaseless tending. In this place, the Slumbering One stirs to nascency, to blossom their flowers throughout the Grand Magasin... in return for the offering that is all that we are.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Yes... The one who shall tend to the Rouges in the absence of our Voice.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: <They haven't been awakened yet, it seems.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I've been humming the most wonderful of lullabies in all of the Grand Magasin. Building the Cradle for the noble one—my magnum opus—weaving it thread by thread, my conviction a weapon against this insatiable hunger...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: So, you're like... What, that thing's nanny, I assume. And it's about to wake soon anyway, innit? What'd it call us here for?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: My role was to be a warm blanket for the Slumbering One. Now that my duty has ended... I will soon meet my end.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: They will be weak upon waking. When the Slumbering One awakens, the gentlest breeze of the Grand Magasin will be as harsh as cutting winds to their skin, while the Noirs, driven by their ignorance and fear, will seek to bury the noble one within the fractures.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: We need your help, strangers.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Soon, their voice shall resonate between the walls of the Grand Magasin... Stay with them... until they can guide us all, with the whole of their body, on how we are to desire...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Hang on a bloody second. You're offloadin' that baby on us, ain't ya? And we're just 'sposed to play nannies for a newborn?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Oi, I don't know about this... We need to get more eyeballs, find our way to the top floor, keep your clock head safe, and escape this hole—we can't take care of a child like that, mate.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Why have you decided to come here, Dante?
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <... To make a different choice.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Is there something I am unaware— ... Are you aware of a piece of knowledge that I am not allowed access?
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <Yeah... Probably.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Does the answer lie... at the terminus of the road this choice will pave?
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <I don't... know.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... It is quite like how Faust operates, your behavior.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Despite not knowing whether this is the right path, you...
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Understood. Faust has no further queries.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Hurry up, what're you bein' so careful for?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <You never know...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Made a clean cut using the Alterationist's pair of scissors.

<color=#ebcaa2>You really want to see where this goes, huh? I guess that's one way to kill time. Doesn't matter; whichever option you end up going with, we'll get a steady supply of Experience Batter.</color>
<... Sounds like she's not so happy we're making a different choice.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... "Sounds like she's not so happy we're making a different choice," said the Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Well... I do wonder that myself.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>I don't know if you recall—who am I kidding? Of course you do—but I often repeat-taste the Canned Stageplay over and over again. I once watched the same Canned Stageplay over 78 times.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Same actions, identical line reads, predictable expressions coming in at moments I'd grown intimately acquainted with... and the same ending I'd watched over a dozen times, followed by a curtain call so familiar it felt like home. All of that soothed my heart. So much so that, when an actor inevitably forgets his line for the nth time, I feel like I have to rush up to the stage and read the line for him.</color>

... I know what stageplay you are referring to. Riddled with blatant inconsistencies in all of its aspects, its central theme and authorial intent were just as incomprehensible as its nonsensical plot.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>That's the one. It was so low-budget that they couldn't afford even a single professional thespian on stage, and the amateurs they hired predictably put out some of the most awkward performances I'd ever seen. It was a terrible Canned Stageplay, by all accounts.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>But... strangely enough, I found myself comforted as I experienced that play.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>No one could understand why I would do such a thing... except you, ma puce.</color>
You get me.
From where the Voice had disappeared,
from the Cradle sectioned open... something crawled out... in the form of a child.
Oi, kid—
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: The child glanced at us in what appeared to be a wary scan. They then carefully lifted themselves, waddled up to the Brand Director, and placed their hand on her body.
Ah... the Slumbering One has awakened.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: The Brand Director spoke, her eyes opening from a deathlike slumber. The child jumped away from her, just as they had from us earlier.
It seemed we weren't the only ones the child was afraid of; they shrank away from everyone and everything.
Many have awaited... your advent...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Uuu...?
We Rouges have given our all... in anticipation of your arrival. And we offer you... what is... and what will be...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Bring them to the Restaurant on the fifth floor, strangers.
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: To speak the true Voice... to mature... the newborn must reach... that floor...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: Please... for... all of us...
texts.speaker: Brand Director

texts.text: She has drawn her final breath, it seems.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Ueh... Uu...
Kid... I can't understand a word of what you're sayin'.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Euh... Uu...
Though the child wasn't really speaking per se, their gestures and the unspoken request gave me a vague sense of what they wanted.
Uu-ah.
The child picked up the piece of the Cradle we had cut off earlier, lifted it to eye level...
Wha... wha' are they doin'? Tryin' to make a weapon out of it?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Perhaps they are merely drawn to observe it, by a spark of curiosity.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Aaaah...
... and opened their mouth. It was uncomfortably wide.
<Um, I think they're trying to... eat it?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: O-oi, stop that! Drop it, kid! It's yucky, you got that? Yucky!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Ee?
That's the last random piece of flesh you're pickin' up from the ground! Give it!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Heathcliff roughly snatched the cut piece of membrane out of the child's hand.
Uunnnhh!!!
<I think you made the kid angry. And scared them at the same time, somehow.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Doubt they'll follow us like that...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Perhaps the cause of alarm can be traced directly back to Heathcliff's theft of the child's "snack."
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: What was I supposed to do, just watch the kid take a big bite out of that chunk of raw flesh? Oi, am I right or what?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Nnnnnuh...!
Wooow. Really, mate? It ain't like I want to bring you along.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <... Heathcliff, why are you arguing with a kid who can't even speak...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Such behavior is a sign of immaturity manifest in adulthood.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Wha— *sigh*
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Heathcliff's eyes went wide with bewilderment. He huffed angrily, glaring back and forth between us and the child.
Alright, fine. Whatever. What're we doin', then? Find some sweets to lure the kid into comin' with us?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: something to appease them so that they'll follow us willingly.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Appease the kid? Here's somethin' you lot don't seem to understand: if you want stubborn kids like 'em to follow you, appeasement ain't gonna cut it.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Might you be... speaking from your own experiences as a youth?
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: <I'm gonna go out on a limb and assume that the "stubborn kid" was yourself.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Shut it, you two. Point is, you've got to teach 'em a lesson that you can't just whinge your way through the world and expect everything to go your way forever. I say we pretend to leave the kid behind, and they'll know to come with.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Without Ryōshū, none of those present were particularly experienced in child-rearing. So...
... the only option we had was to hold our doubts and potential arguments behind our teeth and let Heathcliff try his hand at convincing this child to come with us.
Nuhhh!!! Nnhhh!!!
Right-o, kid. We're about to head out. Stay here or come with—you do whatever you want, I don't care. We're really leavin' now!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: Aah.. eh...?

Heathcliff wheeled around and stomped out of the Cradle, much to the child's apparent surprise. The child turned to us—though I couldn't see their eyes, it was unmistakably a look of confused astonishment.
It was dark outside the Cradle save for a few rays of sunlight that peeked through. From where we stood, it really looked as though Heathcliff had left us for good.
What're you lot faffin' around for? On the double!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: We hurried out of the Cradle as well at Heathcliff's insistence...
Once outside, we peeked surreptitiously between the curtains as the child looked around frantically.
Uu...
Unnnhhh...!
Oi! We're leavin', kid! I ain't playin' around! Cry and throw a tantrum all ya want, I ain't comin' back!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: The child babbled fearfully for a moment, as though they were afraid of the creeping darkness...
Uu... Nnuhhh...!
... then hurriedly toddled toward us, leaving the Cradle behind.
See? That's how you deal with kids.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: ... There is still some distance between us and the child.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Doesn't seem like they're feeling safe sticking with us...
... even though it's pretty obvious that they don't want to be left alone.
<... So we're just walking around like this, I guess?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Nngh...
The corpse of a Rouge. The bladed arms have all been snapped apart, leaving the body sprawled across the floor.
The corpse of a Rouge. The entire body has been crushed beneath a heavy hammer, mangled beyond recognition.
<It's just a corpse.>
The majority of corpses appear to be of the Noirs, Manager. The battle is most likely winding down in the Rouges' favor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... I ain't seein' what's so "luxury" about this place. Sure, it's a bit shiny, but it ain't that posh.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: These items seem to have a more obvious golden glow to them than the items on the other floors. Even the ones that aren't glowing are meticulously decorated, obviously crafted with great care.
... The items here appear to cost significantly more eyeballs than those available on other floors.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Carrying sufficient eyeballs is not enough. The Prestige Tier of the prospective client is also strictly screened before they are permitted to purchase these items.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Oi, Clock.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <Yeah?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Nah. I, hm. I've a bad feelin' about it.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: <What? Bad feeling about what?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Well... seein' as we're here anyway, I'm thinkin'—why don't we just take these and sell 'em on other floors? It ain't like there's anyone watchin' us...
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: That is—
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: I get it, I get it! I was just floatin' the idea, nothin' more. Don't need another shite like that hair coupon incident happenin' again.
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: But I was just about to tell him that was a really good idea...

Ah, well. The display cases seem to be made from pretty durable material anyway.
We decided to move on.
Densely backstitched Golden Hide is visible between layers of fabric.
A display case. Covered in... what appear to be a curtain of flesh.
Oi, oi... you... is your head alright?!
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: It is all right.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <We've got plenty of stuff that might come in helpful, but... still too early to even try to fight it, I guess.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Thin rays of golden light shine from the cracks of the obsidian pillar.
The Noirs have stuffed Le Rouge apparel into the gaps where the Rouges have carved out the Golden Hides.
